title: The Bedroom Where Reginald Mengi Assembled His First Pens
conflicts: Order of events: the 2014 Citizen report of his Forbes Africa interview says the pen idea came after he quit PwC; the 2019 Citizen/EastAfrican pieces drawing on his memoir say he started pens while still at Coopers & Lybrand and left in October 1989; the story follows the memoir and the dated departure. Media dates: Citizen 2014 says Guardian 1994 and ITV a year later (and calls ITV the first TV network); the Media Ownership Monitor gives ITV's start as 10 June 1994 and CTN began earlier, so the story uses 10 June 1994 and does not say 'first'. Age at death 75 (EastAfrican, The National) vs 77 (Citizen 2019): used 75.
notes: Changed episode: the slate's move into media (1993) has no accessible founder account of the decision, so the edition tells the 1983-84 bedroom pen-assembly start (refused $4,000 NBC loan, lorry breakdown at Horohoro) and gives the 1994 media launch as aftermath. Arc changed to founding-decision, industry to manufacturing. The Citizen and The EastAfrican are both Nation Media Group and their 2019 texts overlap; the 'first million within a year' figure is attributed to his memoir.
